unit.label: Afternoon schedules, ongoing actions & routines
unit.title: A Busy Afternoon
unit.description: 13 new words, plus the transparent combinations 每天 and 剛開始. Tell afternoon times, describe ongoing actions, and distinguish every day from not every day.

goal.text: 我每天下午都上書法課。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān xiàwǔ dōu shàng shūfǎ kè.
goal.meaning: I have calligraphy class every afternoon.

unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 7, pp. 135–145. Original examples and exercises.

lessons.title: Just Got Out of Class
lessons.subtitle: Talk about lunch, afternoon, and something that just happened.

steps.prompt: Which phrase means “I just got out of class”?
steps.explanation: 剛 means just now; 下課 means class has finished.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 剛 is gāng, just now.

lessons.title: A Game at 4:30
lessons.subtitle: Use 半 for half past and talk about a competition.

steps.prompt: What time is 四點半?
steps.explanation: 半 after 點 means half past the hour.

steps.prompt: Which word means “game; competition”?
steps.explanation: 比賽 means a game or competition.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 半 is bàn, half.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 賽 is sài, the second character of 比賽.

lessons.title: When Does It End?
lessons.subtitle: Say when an event begins and finishes.

steps.prompt: Which asks when the game ends?
steps.explanation: 結束 means end; 開始 means begin.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 結 is jié in 結束.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 開 is kāi in 開始.

lessons.title: What Are You Doing?
lessons.subtitle: Use 在 before an action that is happening now.

steps.prompt: Which sentence means “I am writing Chinese right now”?
steps.explanation: 在 before the action 寫 marks the action as ongoing.

steps.prompt: Which cannot take progressive 在 in this lesson?
steps.explanation: 忙 is a state verb. Progressive 在 is used with action verbs.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 寫 is xiě, write.

steps.prompt: Which says “They are singing,” rather than naming where they are?
steps.explanation: 在 before 唱歌 marks an ongoing action. 在學校 gives a location; 喜歡 gives a preference.

lessons.title: Every Evening
lessons.subtitle: Use 每…都… for routines and control the scope of negation.

steps.prompt: Which means “I do not have class every day” (not every day)?
steps.explanation: 不是每…都… denies that the statement is true every time.

steps.prompt: Where does 不 go when the negative predicate applies to every weekend?
steps.explanation: The pattern here is 每…都不/沒… .

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 每 is měi, each/every.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 忙 is máng, busy.

steps.prompt: You are free on every weekend, with no busy weekends. Which sentence fits?
options: 我不是每個週末都不忙。
steps.explanation: 都不忙 applies “not busy” to every weekend: never busy on weekends.

steps.prompt: You have classes on some days, but not all days. Which sentence fits?
steps.explanation: 不是每天都 means not every day; 每天都不 would mean no classes on any day.

lessons.title: Calligraphy Class
lessons.subtitle: Combine the new schedule language in a daily routine.

steps.prompt: Which is “calligraphy class”?
steps.explanation: 書法 is calligraphy and 課 is class.

steps.prompt: Which sentence combines a repeated schedule correctly?
options: 我每天下午都上書法課。
我都每天下午書法課上。
steps.answer: 我每天下午都上書法課。
steps.explanation: 每天下午 sets the recurring time; 都 comes before the event.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 法 is fǎ, the second character of 書法.

lessons.title: Unit 22 Review
lessons.subtitle: Afternoon schedules, ongoing actions, and routines.

steps.prompt: Which is 6:30?
steps.explanation: 點半 means half past the hour.

steps.prompt: Which sentence shows an ongoing action?
steps.explanation: 在 directly before an action verb marks the action as ongoing.

steps.prompt: Which means “not every day” rather than “every day not”?
steps.explanation: 不是每…都… denies an all-inclusive claim.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 剛 is gāng.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 賽 is sài.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 寫 is xiě.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 每 is měi.

steps.prompt: 我每個週末都不忙 means:
options: I am never busy on weekends.
I am busy on some weekends but not all.
steps.answer: I am never busy on weekends.
steps.explanation: 每個週末都不忙 makes every weekend a non-busy one.

steps.prompt: Class starts at 2:30. Which sentence fits?
steps.explanation: Match both the event boundary 開始 and the time 兩點半.

newVocabulary.note: Transparent combination explicitly taught here; not an additional independent vocabulary root.

newVocabulary.meaning: to have just started; just beginning
newVocabulary.note: Transparent combination explicitly taught here; not an additional independent vocabulary root.

剛.note: 剛 is first-tone gāng. As an adverb it places an action just before the present moment.
剛.memory: 岡 forms the broad left block and 刂 stands as two knife strokes on the right.

parts.label: 岡
parts.name: left block
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 岡, with an enclosing outer shape around the inner mountain-like strokes.

parts.label: 刂
parts.name: knife component
parts.description: The last two strokes are the narrow vertical knife component on the right.

半.note: 半 is fourth-tone bàn. In clock time, 四點半 means 4:30, literally four o’clock plus half an hour.
半.memory: Two small upper strokes sit above a crossed lower frame; the final vertical runs down through the center.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: two upper strokes
parts.description: Begin with the two short strokes that open above the center.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: crossed lower group
parts.description: The last three strokes make the horizontal framework and central vertical that complete 半.

比.meaning: compare; first character of 比賽
比.note: 比 is third-tone bǐ. In 比賽 it is part of the noun/verb meaning game or competition.
比.memory: Two compact two-stroke shapes sit side by side, like two sides being compared.

parts.label: left
parts.name: left two strokes
parts.description: The first two strokes form the tighter left half.

parts.label: right
parts.name: right two strokes
parts.description: The final two strokes form the right half, ending in the hooked sweep.

賽.note: 賽 is fourth-tone sài. Together with 比 it forms 比賽, “game; competition.”
賽.memory: A roof 宀 covers a dense middle, while traditional 貝 forms the seven-stroke base.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof
parts.description: The first three strokes form the roof across the top of 賽.

parts.label: middle
parts.name: middle crossing group
parts.description: The next seven strokes build the compact crossed middle between the roof and 貝.

parts.label: 貝
parts.name: shell component
parts.description: The final seven strokes form traditional 貝 at the bottom, including the two closing lower strokes.

結.meaning: tie; join; first character of 結束
結.note: 結 is second-tone jié in 結束, “to end; finish.” Keep the traditional silk radical 糹 on the left.
結.memory: The silk radical 糹 stands beside 吉, linking the idea of tying something together.

parts.label: 糹
parts.name: silk component
parts.description: The first six strokes form the traditional silk radical on the left.

parts.label: 吉
parts.name: right block
parts.description: The last six strokes form 吉 on the right, with 士 above 口.

束.meaning: bundle; second character of 結束
束.note: 束 is fourth-tone shù in 結束. This unit learns it inside the common word 結束.
束.memory: A central vertical passes through the boxed middle and opens into two lower strokes, making the whole form look tightly bundled.

parts.label: 束
parts.name: whole bundled form
parts.description: Write the seven-stroke form as one connected design: top horizontal, boxed middle, central vertical, then the two spreading lower strokes.

開.note: 開 is first-tone kāi. In 開始, it helps form the verb “to begin; start.”
開.memory: Traditional 門 forms the outer gate, with the four-stroke inner shape centered inside it.

parts.label: 門
parts.name: gate component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form the traditional 門 frame around the character.

parts.label: 开
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: The final four strokes sit inside the gate as the open inner structure.

始.note: 始 is third-tone shǐ. It appears in 開始, the process verb “to begin; start.”
始.memory: 女 on the left stands beside 台 on the right; keep the lower 口 of 台 compact.

parts.label: 女
parts.name: woman component
parts.description: The first three strokes form the narrow 女 on the left.

parts.label: 台
parts.name: right block
parts.description: The last five strokes form 台 on the right, ending with the three-stroke 口.

寫.note: 寫 is third-tone xiě and is the Traditional form used in Taiwan. It means to write.
寫.memory: A roof 宀 sits above the dense 舄-shaped lower block; the four dots anchor the bottom.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof
parts.description: The first three strokes form the roof across the top.

parts.label: 舄
parts.name: lower block
parts.description: The remaining twelve strokes make the dense lower block, ending with the four bottom dots.

忙.note: 忙 is second-tone máng. It is a state verb meaning busy.
忙.memory: The heart radical 忄 stands on the left of 亡; picture a heart pulled in many directions.

parts.label: 忄
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: The first three strokes form the narrow heart radical on the left.

parts.label: 亡
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last three strokes form 亡 on the right, with the dot over its horizontal frame.

每.note: 每 is third-tone měi. It introduces each/every and is normally paired with 都 in the sentence pattern taught here.
每.memory: Two short upper strokes sit over a 母-like lower box; keep the central crossing lines clear.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper strokes
parts.description: The first two strokes form the short top of 每.

parts.label: 母
parts.name: lower mother-like form
parts.description: The last five strokes form the boxed, crossed lower shape related visually to 母.

法.meaning: method; law; second character of 書法
法.note: 法 is third-tone fǎ. In 書法 it refers to the art/method of writing: calligraphy.
法.memory: Three water dots 氵 sit beside 去; keep the left dots light and the right side compact.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: The first three strokes are the water radical along the left edge.

parts.label: 去
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 去 on the right, with 土 above the bent lower strokes.

u22-half-time.title: Say half past with 半
u22-half-time.explanation: Place 半 after 點 to mean half past the hour. 四點半 is 4:30 and 六點半 is 6:30. This extends the clock-time pattern from Unit 21.
u22-half-time.remember: Use 點半 for :30. Do not add 分 after 半.

u22-event-start-end.title: Say when an event starts or ends
u22-event-start-end.pattern: Event + Time + 開始 / 結束
u22-event-start-end.explanation: 開始 marks the beginning of an event and 結束 marks its end. To ask, put 幾點 before 開始 or 結束: 比賽幾點結束？ The event is the topic and the clock time tells when the change happens.

examples.pinyin: Bǐsài xiàwǔ sì diǎn bàn kāishǐ.
examples.meaning: The game starts at 4:30 in the afternoon.
What time does the game end?

u22-event-start-end.remember: 開始 = begin; 結束 = finish/end. Use the clock time before the process verb.

u22-progressive-zai.title: Show an action in progress with 在
u22-progressive-zai.explanation: Before an action verb, 在 marks an activity that is ongoing at the relevant time. This is different from locative 在 + place. Only action verbs work in this progressive pattern. When correcting a mistaken ongoing action, 不是在… is common.

examples.text: 他不是在看書，他在寫中文。
examples.pinyin: Tā bú shì zài kàn shū, tā zài xiě Zhōngwén.
examples.meaning: He is not reading; he is writing Chinese.

u22-progressive-zai.remember: 在 + place = be at a place. 在 + action verb = action in progress. Do not use progressive 在 with state verbs such as 忙 or 貴.

u22-every-dou.title: Every… with 每…都…
u22-every-dou.explanation: 每 means each/every. The sentence normally includes 都 to reinforce that there are no exceptions. With common time words, 一 can be omitted: 每天 = 每一天, and 每個週末 = every weekend.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi ge zhōumò dōu bù máng.
examples.meaning: I am never busy on weekends.

u22-every-dou.remember: Think 每…都… as “every… all/no exceptions.” Put 都 before the predicate.

u22-every-negation.title: Negation inside and outside 每…都…
u22-every-negation.pattern: 每…都不/沒…  vs.  不是每…都…
u22-every-negation.explanation: To say the predicate is negative on every occasion, put 不 or 沒 after 都: 每…都不…. To deny that something is true without exception, place 不是 before 每: 不是每…都…, meaning “not every…”. The scope is different.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi ge zhōumò dōu bù máng.
examples.meaning: I am never busy on weekends.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú shì měitiān dōu shàngkè.
examples.meaning: I do not have class every day.

u22-every-negation.remember: 都不 = all are not / always not. 不是每…都… = not every one / not always.

u22-just-class.meaning: I just got out of class.
u22-just-class.note: 剛 places 下課 immediately before now.

u22-lunch.note: 午餐 is lunch; 中午 is the time of day.

u22-afternoon.meaning: I go to school in the afternoon.
u22-afternoon.note: 下午 is a time expression and comes before the event.

u22-game-time.pinyin: Wǒ xiàwǔ sì diǎn bàn yǒu bǐsài.
u22-game-time.meaning: I have a game at 4:30 in the afternoon.

u22-game-start.pinyin: Bǐsài xiàwǔ sì diǎn bàn kāishǐ.
u22-game-start.meaning: The game starts at 4:30 in the afternoon.
u22-game-start.note: The game is the topic; the time comes before 開始.

u22-game-end.note: 結束 is the endpoint process.

u22-end-question.meaning: What time does the game end?
u22-end-question.note: 幾點 asks for the clock time.

u22-writing.note: Here 在 marks an ongoing action, not a location.

u22-basketball-now.note: 在 comes directly before the action phrase.

u22-correct-action.text: 他不是在看書，他在寫中文。
u22-correct-action.pinyin: Tā bú shì zài kàn shū, tā zài xiě Zhōngwén.
u22-correct-action.meaning: He is not reading; he is writing Chinese.
u22-correct-action.note: 不是在… corrects a mistaken claim about the ongoing action.

u22-busy.note: 忙 is a state verb, so do not put progressive 在 before it.

u22-every-evening.note: 每 sets the repeated time and 都 reinforces no exception.

u22-not-every.pinyin: Wǒ bú shì měitiān dōu shàngkè.
u22-not-every.meaning: I do not have class every day.
u22-not-every.note: 不是每…都… means the statement is not true every time.

u22-every-not-busy.pinyin: Wǒ měi ge zhōumò dōu bù máng.
u22-every-not-busy.meaning: I am never busy on weekends.
u22-every-not-busy.note: 不 follows 都 because the negative predicate applies to every weekend.

u22-calligraphy.text: 我每天下午都上書法課。
u22-calligraphy.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān xiàwǔ dōu shàng shūfǎ kè.
u22-calligraphy.meaning: I have calligraphy class every afternoon.
u22-calligraphy.note: 書法課 is a calligraphy class.

u22-start-study.note: 剛 modifies the process 開始.

u22-like-writing.note: 寫 is an action verb; 中文 is its object.
